p: between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua
regarding "an assembly to Hashem your God" (Devarim 16:8)
and "an assembly shall it be for you" (Bamidbar 29:35):
half of it for Hashem and half of it for you,
either all of it for Hashem
or all of it for you.
And seemingly, what reason is there
Let us say each one as its own law:
that is, on the seventh day of Pesach,
and on the day of Shemini Atzeres, "for you,"
that it be all of it for you.
And one may say, on a plain level,
that we learn one from the other
in the way that we find
that we derive a gezeirah shavah
to apply what is said of this one to that one.
And this is known from the Rambam, z"l
that the learning of a gezeirah shavah
is called "from the words of the Soferim."
And in the essence of the matter,
that the root of the holiness of the festival of Pesach
as is known from their saying, z"l
that with leaven, a little is good.
That is, the yetzer hara of desire,
which is the leaven in the dough,
one needs to make use of it
However, it is known from the Rambam, z"l
has fallen ill with a sickness of the soul
he needs to distance himself from it
And this is the matter of the festival of Pesach,
in which we go out from the depths of lowliness;
and for this one needs to distance oneself
in order to repair the first damage,
which sprang from the desire for eating,
שְׂאוֹר לֹא יִמָּצֵא בְּבָתֵּיכֶם (שְׁמוֹת יב, יט).
"Leaven shall not be found in your houses" (Shemos 12:19).
And also in the mitzvah of eating matzah
to distance oneself from the taste of the chametz
And therefore it says of it,
for on the level of the outer garment,
to distance oneself from the pleasures of this world,
so that one only sits and learns.
it is in the aspect of "for you,"
which comes through "to Hashem your God."
engaging in Torah and mitzvos in actual deed
a feeling of pleasure to the body;
in the name of the holy Rav of Lublin,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing for the life of the World to Come,
who said of a certain man
that he received from learning Torah.
which comes after the festival of Sukkos,
that precisely through eating and drinking
the repair of the blemish of desire is made.
For this is the special power of the mitzvah of sukkah:
in nullifying the yetzer hara of desire,
regarding the Men of the Great Assembly
that it shielded them like a sukkah.
we recite the blessing "to dwell in the sukkah"
the essence of the mitzvah of sukkah:
to refine the desire for eating in holiness.
And alluding to this they said, z"l
on which the Torah was given."
That is, at the time of the giving of the Torah
a nullification of the yetzer hara,
which was uprooted from their hearts, as is known.
And through the gezeirah shavah we learn
we come to "to Hashem your God":
"And drink your wine with a good heart."
That is, from the wine of the Torah,
"And drink of the wine that I have mixed";
and it does not say "of my wine,"
only that there is drawn into it, hidden,
the power of His providence, Yisbarach,
And that is how, through the "for you,"
we come to "to Hashem your God," as mentioned above.
